question.text: Under Section 39(7) of the Insurance Act, 1938 (as amended in 2015), which of the following nominees of a life-insurance policyholder is classified as a "Beneficial Nominee" who is beneficially entitled to the insurance proceeds rather than holding them in trust for the legal heirs?

answer.text: A business partner of the policyholder
A friend named in the will of the policyholder

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B (p.28), Section 39(7) of the Insurance Act, 1938 states that where the nominee of a life-insurance policyholder is the parent, spouse, children, the spouse and children, or any of them, the nominee is beneficially entitled to the insurance amount. Per p.54, the workbook reiterates that the spouse, parent, children, or any combination thereof inherit beneficially rather than as trustees of the legal heirs. The Trap: A sibling, business partner, or friend is not within the parent/spouse/children category that Section 39(7) recognises as beneficial nominees. Such a nominee receives the proceeds but holds them in trust for the legal heirs under general nomination principles. Note: The beneficial-nominee exception is specifically carved out for the parent/spouse/children class; all other nominees fall back to the general rule.
